(2) Frontend Playwright e2e on the LIVE preview URL: full printer checkout flow (Mumbai vs dealer Bengaluru) → Step 2 shows summary-delivery=₹350, summary-total=₹18,050 (subtotal 15000 + GST 2700 + 350), 'Place Order' returned 200 and landed on /order-confirmed/<orderId>. action_items: Already fixed by testing agent: added _resolve_delivery_charge to the underscore-helpers import in /app/backend/routes/orders.py (was crashing all toner order placements with NameError 500). Verify the fix in main agent's next code review and keep in mind that `from server import *` does NOT pull underscore-prefixed kernel helpers — they must be listed explicitly in routes/*.py imports.
critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL (fixed): routes/orders.py used _resolve_delivery_charge on line 53 (toner path) but never imported it. Because Python's `from module import *` ignores names starting with `_`, the symbol was undefined at runtime and every toner POST /api/orders crashed with 500 NameError. This is a recurring footgun for this codebase — every new underscore-prefixed helper added to server.py MUST be added to the explicit underscore-helpers import line of every route module that uses it.

computeCartDelivery in /app/frontend/src/lib/delivery.js correctly mirrors the backend resolver and the 'charge once per dealer, highest category rate' rule — verified live with a 2-item single-dealer (printer+toner) cart returning ₹350, not ₹450.

Checkout.jsx hardcodes a default kind='toner' in the order payload (`it.product?.kind || 'toner'`) — fine today because PrinterProductCard / ProductDetail now stamp kind correctly, but if a future card forgets to stamp kind it will silently default to the wrong category. Consider raising a console.warn when kind is missing.

Backend server.py _resolve_delivery_charge (line 423) is authoritative and ignores client-sent delivery_charge — confirmed: client sent 999, server stored 350 for intercity / 0 for same-city across every category.

rca of the issue: RCA — toner orders 500: routes/orders.py imports kernel helpers from server.py via `from server import *` (which excludes underscore names per Python spec) plus an explicit `from server import (_helper1, _helper2, ...)` list. When Wave 22 added _resolve_delivery_charge to server.py and wired it into the toner branch of create_order, the explicit underscore-helpers import line was not updated. Reproduction: POST /api/orders with listing_kind=toner and any valid toner listing_id → 500 with traceback 'NameError: name _resolve_delivery_charge is not defined' at orders.py:53. Backend logs at /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log show the stack trace. Mitigation applied: added `_resolve_delivery_charge` to the explicit-import tuple on line 14 of routes/orders.py. Re-tested — all 15 wave22 tests pass.
